As a junior he was named a third team [[All-American]] by the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] and the [[Sporting News]].[http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/032813aaa.html Men's Basketball's Smith Earns NABC All-America Honors][http://www.whas11.com/sports/Russ-Smith-named-Sporting-News-All-American-197233781.html Russ Smith named Sporting News All-American] ==High School== Smith was born in [[New York City]] and went to [[Archbishop Molloy High School]] in Queens, N.Y. and played basketball for head coach [[Jack Curran]]. He led the New York City Catholic league ([[CHSAA]]) in scoring as a junior averaging 24.5 points a game and as a senior averaging 29.6 points,{{cite web|last=Winn|first=Luke|title=11 Russdiculous facts about Louisville's Russ Smith|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/college-basketball/news/20121221/russ-smith-louisville/|work=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com|publisher=Sports Illustrated|accessdate=1 April 2013}} he also had a 7.3 rebound and 3.2 assist average his final season for the Molloy Stanners. His career high in points was 47, which he reached twice as a senior against St. Francis Prep and Christ the King. Smith was named to the 2009 New York State Sportswriters Association all-state team, made the first-team all-CHSAA "AA", and New York Daily News All-Queens first team as a senior. He played in the 2009 [[Jordan Brand Classic]] Regional Game at Madision Square Garden on April 18. Where he scored 27 points and earned co-MVP honors as his City team beat the Suburban team 129–120. Russ played prep school basketball at [[South Kent School]] in 2010 averaging 19.7 points and 3.9 assists a game as South Kent went 20–12 on the season.{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Russ|title=Russ Smith Bio|url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/russ_smith_729175.html|work=http://www.gocards.com|publisher=Louisville Cardinals|accessdate=31 March 2013}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2010}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Russ Smith | position = G | hometown = Brooklyn, NY | highschool = Archbishop Molloy High School, NY
South Kent School, CT | feet = 6 | inches = 0 | weight = 165 | 40 = | commitdate = 11/15/2009 | scout stars = 2 | rivals stars = 3 | espn grade = 88 }} |} ==College== ===Recruitment=== Louisville overlooked Smith at first, assistant coach [[Steve Masiello]] who had known Russ's father since he was 15, ended up getting Russ to commit to the Cardinals. Assistant coach [[Ralph Willard]] was on a recruiting trip with Masiello at South Kent in September 2009 looking at another player. Willard thought Smith would be perfect for their system, only after that did Louisville start looking at Smith seriously. Smith liked Louisville so much he tried to commit before he had a scholarship offer. Houston, LaSalle, Baylor and Arizona showed interest before he signed with the Cardinals. ===Freshman year=== Injuries limited Smith's playing time as a freshman. He had a broken foot, concussion, strained foot, and sore knee during the season and only saw action in 17 games. Smith was so miserable with the injuries and lack of playing time he decided to leave Louisville and go back home. He had even called his mom and told her he was coming home. But that day against West Virginia, coach Pitino put him in and told him to play hard. He had 3 points, 2 rebounds, one steal, and played good defense in his nine minutes of action.{{cite web|author=7:00 PM ET, January 26, 2011KFC Yum! Center, Louisville, KY |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=310260097 |title=West Virginia Mountaineers vs. Louisville Cardinals – Box Score – January 26, 2011 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2011-01-26 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Helping spark the Cardinals' comeback from down 11 to win by 1, when [[Peyton Siva]] hit a layup at the buzzer.{{cite web|author=7:00 PM ET, January 26, 2011KFC Yum! Center, Louisville, KY |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310260097 |title=West Virginia Mountaineers vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap – January 26, 2011 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2011-01-26 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} After that, he decided to stay. The Cardinals reached the championship game of the [[2011 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament]] but lost to [[2010–11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]].{{cite web|title=2011–12 Louisville Basketball Media Guide|url=http://www.guide.provations.com/louisville/2011mensbasketball#pg64|work=Player Bio: Peyton Siva|publisher=University of Louisville|accessdate=29 January 2012}} Louisville finished the season 25–10, 12–6 in the [[2010–11 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2010–11 Big East season]] tied for 3rd in the conference. They received an at-large bid and a #4 seed in the [[2011 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2011 NCAA Tournament]] where they were upset in the second round by #13 seeded [[2010–11 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] 61–62.{{cite web|author=1:40 PM ET, March 17, 2011Pepsi Center, Denver, CO |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310760097 |title=Morehead State Eagles vs. Louisville Cardinals – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – March 17, 2011 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2011-03-17 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} ===Sophomore year=== During his sophomore year in [[2011-12 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2011–12]], Smith provided a spark off the bench. He was second in scoring despite being sixth in mins played for the Cardinals.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/team/stats/_/id/97/year/2012/louisville-cardinals |title=Louisville Cardinals 2011–12 Statistics – Team and Player Stats – Men's College Basketball – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date= |accessdate=2013-04-09}} In January 2012 he earned the nickname "Russdiculous" given to him by head coach [[Rick Pitino]], who has named a race horse "Russdiculous" also.{{cite web|author=Luke Winn |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1206631/1/index.htm |title=DO WHAT YOU WANT. SWAGG ALL THE TIME. LOUISVILLE GUARD – 12.24.12 – SI Vault |publisher=Sportsillustrated.cnn.com |date=2012-12-24 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Smith set a school record for steals in a season with 87 steals in his 39 games played. Louisville won four games in four nights to win the [[2012 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|2012 Big East tournament Championship]]. The Cardinals advanced to the Final Four of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]], upsetting #1 seed [[2011–12 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 57–44 in the sweet sixteen and defeating #7 seed [[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the regional final, where Smith led Louisville with 19 points in the game.{{cite web|author=4:30 PM ET, March 24, 2012US Airways Center, Phoenix, AZ |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=320840097 |title=Florida Gators vs. Louisville Cardinals – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – March 24, 2012 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2012-03-24 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Before losing in the national semifinals to [[Kentucky–Louisville rivalry|arch-rival]] and eventual national champion [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. Smith averaged 11.5 points, 2.5 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 2.2 steals a game for the Cardinals, who finished the season with a 30–10 record.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/51478/year/2012/russ-smith |title=Russ Smith Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=1991-04-19 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} ===Junior year=== [[Image:Russ Smith Peyton Siva championship trophy.jpg|thumb|right|Smith (left) and [[Peyton Siva]] (right) with the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] trophy.]] Before the start of the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 basketball season]] the [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team]] was picked to finish 1st in the [[2012–13 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East Conference]] in polls done by Big East writers {{cite web|author=Central New York |url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/10/louisville_tops_big_east_write.html |title=Louisville tops Big East writers' poll; Cardinals dominate all-league teams |publisher=syracuse.com |date= |accessdate=2013-04-09}} and coaches.{{cite web|last=Smith |first=Jared |url=http://newyork.sbnation.com/2012/10/17/3517762/big-east-basketball-media-day-2012-coaches-poll-all-big-east-preseason |title=Big East basketball media day: Coaches' poll, All-Big East preseason teams and news – SB Nation New York |publisher=Newyork.sbnation.com |date=2012-10-17 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Louisville finished the regular season with a 26–5 record and 14–4 in the Big East to tie for a share of the Big East regular season championship with [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] and [[2012–13 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]], who also finished with a 14–4 conference record.{{cite web|last=Ennis |first=Mark |url=http://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2013/3/12/4091940/2013-big-east-tournament-preview-louisville-georgetown-syracuse-otto-porter |title=2013 Big East Tournament preview: Louisville and Georgetown favorites in league's swan song |publisher=SBNation.com |date=2013-03-12 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Smith learned about the death of his high school coach Jack Curran before the start of the [[2013 Big East Men's Basketball Tournament|2013 Big East Tournament]]. Louisville played [[2012–13 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in their first game of the tournament, Smith scored 28 points and said "Today was definitely Coach Curran Day for me, and it will be the rest of my life" in postgame interview that aired live on [[ESPN]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330730097 |title=Villanova Wildcats vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap – March 14, 2013 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2013-03-14 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Russ was named to the Big East All-Tournament Team{{cite web|last=Mike|first=Waters|title=Louisville's Peyton Siva joins Georgetown's Patrick Ewing as the only two-time winners of the Big East Most Outstanding Player award|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/03/louisvilles_peyton_siva_joins.html|work=syracuse.com|publisher=The Post Standars|accessdate=17 March 2013}} and his team won the Big East Tournament Championship game versus [[2012-13 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] by a score of 78–61 after trailing by 13 at halftime.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330750097 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap – March 16, 2013 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2013-03-16 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Louisville, with a 29–5 record, was selected the #1 overall seed for the [[2013 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2013 NCAA Tournament]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/9063277/2013-ncaa-tournament-louisville-cardinals-named-top-overall-seed |title=2013 NCAA tournament – Louisville Cardinals named top overall seed – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2013-03-26 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} In his first two games of the NCAA tournament at [[Rupp Arena]] he had 23 points verses [[2012–13 North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball team|North Carolina A&T]] and had 27 against [[2012–13 Colorado State Rams men's basketball team|Colorado State]]. Louisville fans liked what Russ was doing on the floor so much they started chanting RussArena{{cite web|author=5:15 PM ET, March 23, 2013Rupp Arena, Lexington, KY |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330820097 |title=Colorado State Rams vs. Louisville Cardinals – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – March 23, 2013 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2013-03-23 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} near the end of the Colorado State game and made a Twitter hashtag #RussArena.{{cite web|author=Tommy Tomlinson |url=http://www.sportsonearth.com/article/43306768/ |title=Russ Smith could be the key to Louisville's Final Four run. | SportsonEarth.com : Tommy Tomlinson Article |publisher=SportsonEarth.com |date=2013-03-26 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} He tied his career high of 31 points and the Cardinals beat the [[2012-13 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon Ducks]] 77–69 in the Sweet Sixteen.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330880097 |title=Oregon Ducks vs. Louisville Cardinals – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – March 29, 2013 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2013-03-29 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} In Louisville's 85–63 regional final win against [[2012-13 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], Smith recorded 23 points and was subsequently named the Most Outstanding Player of the tournament's Midwest Region. During the Duke game Smith witnessed [[Kevin Ware]] suffer a horrible broken leg accident that left the team very emotional. Ware said "Just go win this game for me. Just go win this game. Don't worry about me, I'm fine." while being attended to by medical staff who was preparing him for a trip to the hospital. Louisville outscored Duke 64 to 43 after the Ware injury and credited Ware's positive attitude about his injury for their win.{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330900097|title=Emotional Louisville overcomes injury to Kevin Ware to reach Final Four|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} In Louisville's next game Smith had 21 points in a 72–68 win over [[2012–13 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]] in the Final Four.{{cite web|author=6:09 PM ET, April 6, 2013Georgia Dome, Atlanta, GA |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330960097 |title=Wichita State Shockers vs. Louisville Cardinals – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – April 06, 2013 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=2012-01-01 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} Smith averaged 18.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 2.1 steals this season for the Cardinals who won the national championship over Michigan with a 35–5 record.{{cite web|author=Mon, Apr 8 |url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/51478/russ-smith |title=Russ Smith Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=1991-04-19 |accessdate=2013-04-09}} ===Senior year=== On April 24, 2013, Smith announced he would stay at Louisville for his senior year. On February 28, he was named one of the 10 semi-finalists for [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by
